extracted.intended_audience: novelists and screenwriters adapting a novel into a screenplay
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for compressing a novel’s narrative, characters, and internal material into a film-ready screenplay that emphasizes visual storytelling, pace, and structure. Covers selection of elements to keep/cut, converting internal monologue, dialogue crafting, non-linear handling, and revision/feedback processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure: From Expansive to Concise
rubrics_metrics.description: Novels often embrace complexity, exploring themes and developing settings in detail; screenplays prioritize visual storytelling over descriptive text and require distilling vast narrative content into a lean, efficient format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert paragraphs of description into concise scene headings and minimal action lines. Focus on what is necessary to convey setting and tone on screen; remove excess exposition that slows cinematic pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling: Visual vs. Internal
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelists can explore characters’ thoughts and emotions internally; scripts must translate those internal narratives into visual terms—showing rather than telling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rethink story elements so dialogue and action carry the story. Avoid internal monologue except when absolutely necessary; instead express interiority through behavior, visuals, and subtext.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing: Reader-Controlled vs. Real-Time
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers control pacing in novels (lingering or skimming); films unfold in real time and are typically constrained to a 90–120 minute runtime, requiring efficient scene structuring and pacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each scene serves a purpose and advances the narrative. Trim scenes that add length without propulsion. Use variation in scene length and balance suspenseful and quieter moments to maintain momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying Core Themes and Plot Points
rubrics_metrics.description: Distill the novel’s main themes and plot points; define what makes the story unique and which elements are integral for the screen adaptation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain elements that are essential to the protagonist’s arc and the novel’s core message. Use this distillation to decide which subplots or scenes can be omitted or condensed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlining Characters and Subplots
rubrics_metrics.description: Films have less time to develop many characters and subplots; you must examine which characters are essential and which can be combined or cut.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider combining roles into composite characters or eliminating less impactful ones to avoid bloating the script. Keep only characters that forward the plot or enrich the main storyline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Cinematic Techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Use film-specific devices (visual symbols, setting changes, flashbacks, montages) rather than relying on prose to convey information and emotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate information into visual shorthand—symbols, recurring motifs, montage sequences, or setting-driven reveals—to preserve depth without lengthy exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing Tone and Setting (Opening Scene)
rubrics_metrics.description: The opening scene should visually articulate the setting and establish a tone aligned with the novel’s intent, offering a snapshot of the film’s world without lengthy exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use atmospheric music, sweeping landscapes, or a day-in-the-life sequence to immerse viewers immediately. Show, don’t tell—convey the world succinctly in images and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hook the Audience (Opening Scene)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with a strong hook—an intriguing action, dramatic moment, or unusual scenario—that raises questions and engages viewers emotionally right away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open on a scene that sets character and stakes immediately (example: Raiders of the Lost Ark’s booby-trapped temple). Use immediate momentum to encourage audience investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embracing the Three-Act Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the three-act structure—setup, confrontation, resolution—to provide coherent pacing and narrative progression suitable for film.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act One (Setup): introduce characters, setting, and main conflict; Act Two (Confrontation): escalate challenges and weave subplots while staying focused on central themes; Act Three (Resolution): resolve conflict and character arcs for a satisfying conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining Pacing and Emotional Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each act and scene should transition smoothly to keep viewers engaged; pacing affects emotional investment and the film’s rhythm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary scene lengths, alternate suspenseful and quieter beats, and ensure scenes carry emotional stakes. Keep audience engagement by preventing lulls and unnecessary exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinventing Key Moments with Climactic Arcs
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify pivotal moments in the novel and adapt them into climactic scenes that highlight the story’s strongest emotional beats for visual impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fine-tune these arcs to suit cinematic rhythm while remaining true to emotional truth. Adapt or condense scenarios for maximum visual and emotional resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual Storytelling (Converting Internal Monologues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey characters’ internal thoughts and emotions visually through actions, symbols, settings, and cinematic framing instead of inner narration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use visual metaphors, environment, and cinematography to externalize internal states. Design shots and sequences that communicate subtext without explicit internal monologue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions and Expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace pages of internal monologue with specific physical actions and expressive detail that reveal character states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show hesitation, nervousness, or joy through small, specific behaviors (fidgeting, pacing, facial micro-expressions) and use close-ups for intimacy and emotional clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtext in Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialogue can imply internal thoughts through what is not said—lines that mean one thing on the surface while implying another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft lines that carry double meaning; let subtext provide emotional depth. Use implication and restraint rather than explicit statements of feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisp and Natural Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Screenplay dialogue should be concise and focused on advancing plot or revealing character, sounding natural when spoken aloud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim superfluous words from novel dialogue. Read lines aloud to ensure they feel natural; give each character a distinct voice consistent with the source material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining Depth (Dialogue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even condensed dialogue should respect the original narrative’s depth, encapsulating tension, theme, or character growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place dialogue strategically to echo themes or mark character development. Use silences and pauses as meaningful beats that can convey more than words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Context and Setting (to Support Dialogue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Context cues and physical setting can reinforce dialogue and add layers of meaning without extra lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use props, locations, and staging to support what characters say; let environment amplify subtext and provide narrative context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Techniques for Clarity (Non-linear Narratives)
rubrics_metrics.description: When adapting non-linear novels, use clear cinematic devices (flashbacks, flashforwards, distinct visual cues) so audiences can follow time shifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make each time shift purposeful and visually distinct through lighting, color grading, or sound design. Avoid confusing or gratuitous jumps; each shift should add narrative or emotional value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage Through Structure (Handling Non-linear Plots)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use structural techniques like parallel editing to juxtapose different timelines or storylines and create thematic or emotional connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Juxtapose scenes from different times to highlight contrasts or parallels. Ensure editing choices build suspense or deepen understanding rather than merely complicating chronology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining Emotional Resonance (Non-linear Work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-linear adaptation must still preserve clear emotional arcs so the audience experiences a coherent emotional journey despite time shifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each segment—past, present, future—contributes to the central characters’ emotional development. Keep emotional through-lines consistent across timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engaging Professional Feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek objective assessments from professional script readers or analysts who evaluate structure, character development, pacing, and dialogue against industry standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use professional notes to identify structural weaknesses and opportunities. Consider paid coverage or script analysis to get industry-aligned critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative Workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in workshops to receive peer feedback and varied interpretations that can reveal blind spots or inspire solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share drafts in supportive groups, treat feedback as exploratory, and note recurring issues raised by multiple readers as priorities for revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative Revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat feedback as a dialogue and iterate—incorporate suggestions that align with your vision while making changes that strengthen clarity and emotional impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise multiple drafts, testing changes for clarity, pacing, and emotional resonance. Use each iteration to tighten scenes, deepen characters, and refine cinematic translation from the novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging & Seeking Opportunities (Next Steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: After polishing the adaptation, share it with contests, agents, or production companies to pursue production opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research appropriate contests, submission guidelines, and industry contacts; tailor submission materials and consider professional coverage or query strategies to attract interest.
